Bulgaria has launched a digital nomad visa: starting from €31,000 per year, offering Schengen access and the Euro

Bulgaria introduced a separate type of residency for digital nomads. The scheme is designed for citizens from countries outside the EU, EEA, and Switzerland: live in the country and work remotely without a Bulgarian employer and local clients.

The norm was incorporated in amendments to the foreigners' law. The goal is to attract specialists in IT, innovation, and creative industries. The breakdown was published by BGNES on August 21, referencing an analysis by Alex Ledson in Forbes.

- remote employees of companies outside the EU/EEA/Switzerland;
- owners and partners of certain foreign companies;
- freelancers and independent specialists if the activity is conducted outside Bulgaria.

It is not allowed to provide services to Bulgarian individuals or organizations with this status.

Applicants must demonstrate an average income for the previous calendar year of not less than 50 times the Bulgarian minimum wage. In 2026, this is around €31,000.

Additionally, proof of remote work, accommodation in Bulgaria, health insurance, and a police clearance certificate are required.

The process involves two steps:
1. first, apply for a national D visa in a consulate abroad;
2. after entry, submit an application for a digital nomad residency permit within 14 days.

The permit is issued for 1 year, with the possibility of extension for another year. The two-step process is more complex than some European programs where everything is processed in one application.

### Why go
According to Eurostat data for 2025, consumer prices in Bulgaria are 63% of the EU average, the lowest in the Union (behind Romania and Poland).

From January 1, 2025, the country is fully in the Schengen Area, and land border controls with neighboring countries are lifted. From January 1, 2026, Bulgaria is in the eurozone.

The internet is stable. Remote workers are already in Sofia, Plovdiv, and Bansko: mountains, sea, cheaper than Lisbon and Barcelona.

The downside is the same: two stages required and it's not allowed to work on the Bulgarian market. For those who already earn "from outside," this is more of a status limitation than an income loophole.

📌 Bonding Curves: How Token Prices Move With Every Buy and Sell

Main Points
⏺ Bonding curves define a token’s price as a math function of supply
⏺ Every buy pushes the price up along the curve; every sell pushes it down
⏺ This post explains why bonding curves are popular for launches and micro-caps

1️⃣ Core Concept — instead of an order book, a smart contract sets the price based on how many tokens are already minted or held.
2️⃣ Automatic Pricing — early buyers get cheaper tokens; as demand increases, the curve raises the price automatically.
3️⃣ Liquidity Built-In — the contract always stands ready to buy back tokens along the same curve, so there’s no traditional LP needed.
4️⃣ Design Choices — steeper curves pump price faster but are more volatile; flatter curves are smoother but less “explosive.”
5️⃣ Risks — thin real liquidity, manipulation, and the fact that math-driven pricing doesn’t guarantee real fundamental value.

Final Thoughts

Bonding curves turn token price into a formula instead of a market guess — transparent, but still only as meaningful as the demand behind it.

📌 Grayscale launches first Zcash ETF with direct ZEC exposure 

🔖 Grayscale has launched the first exchange-traded fund offering direct exposure to Zcash, bringing the privacy-focused cryptocurrency to NYSE Arca under the ticker ZCSH. Grayscale said Tuesday that the Zcash ETF began trading as a conversion of its existing Grayscale Zcash Trust, giving investors access to ZEC through an exchange-traded product without requiring them to directly hold the cryptocurrency. 

🌐 The fund carries a 2.5% annual sponsor fee. A Grayscale spokesperson said revenue collected from the fee will be directed back into the Zcash ecosystem to support network development, marketing and other initiatives tied to the cryptocurrency. Zcash, launched in 2016, allows users to make shielded transactions that can conceal transaction information through zero-knowledge proofs. The ETF itself holds ZEC while its shares trade through the traditional securities market.

🔗 Grayscale’s launch follows a regulatory process that began with plans to convert its long-running Zcash Trust into an exchange-traded product. Grayscale later submitted several amendments as it moved the registration process forward. Its fifth amended filing, submitted before the weekend ahead of Tuesday’s launch, set the annual sponsor fee at 2.5% and finalized additional terms for the fund.

📌 What is RSI? The overbought/oversold indicator explained 

🔖 The relative strength index is one of the most widely used momentum oscillators in crypto trading, but most traders misread what it actually measures. This guide breaks down the RSI formula, explains how overbought and oversold signals work in practice, and covers the mistakes that turn a useful indicator into a losing strategy. Most traders learn RSI backwards. They start with the idea that 70 means “sell” and 30 means “buy,” treating the indicator like a traffic light for entries and exits. That mental model sounds logical, but it ignores what RSI actually calculates. The relative strength index does not measure whether an asset is expensive or cheap.

🌐 It measures how aggressively price has been moving in one direction compared to the other. Understanding that distinction is the difference between using RSI as a crutch and using it as a genuine analytical tool. RSI quantifies momentum by comparing the average size of recent up moves to the average size of recent down moves over a defined lookback period. The default period is 14, meaning the calculation considers the last 14 candles on whatever timeframe you are viewing.

📊 Average gain is the sum of all positive price changes over the lookback period divided by N. Average loss is the sum of all negative price changes (expressed as positive numbers) divided by N. Periods with no change count as zero for both. What this produces is a bounded oscillator. When gains completely dominate losses, RS becomes very large and RSI approaches 100. When losses dominate, RS approaches zero and RSI drops toward 0. A perfect balance between gains and losses produces an RS of 1 and an RSI of 50.
